name: Witch Doctor: Amphibimorph breaks on damage and caps its player duration at 8 sec (#934)
contract: Amphibimorph 500952 (SpellFamilyName 19, Mechanic 17 MECHANIC_POLYMORPH) is DBC-native for its frog transform (aura 56), attack/cast lockout (aura 60) and 25% slow (aura 33) - no module code is needed for those and the issue's claim of 'no mechanical effect' is wrong. Two tooltip clauses were genuinely missing before this fix: 'Damage caused may interrupt the effect' (AuraInterruptFlags was 524288 / 0x80000 CHANGE_MAP only, missing 0x2 AURA_INTERRUPT_FLAG_TAKE_DAMAGE - confirmed against the live Spell.dbc record) and '(8 sec vs players)' (GetDiminishingReturnsLimitDuration in SpellMgr.cpp had no case for family 19 / id 500952, so it fell through to the generic 10 s PvP cap instead of 8 s). The fix adds an AscensionWitchDoctor::ApplyContracts clause (AscensionWitchDoctorCompletion.cpp, same pattern as the existing Hexed clause) that ORs AURA_INTERRUPT_FLAG_TAKE_DAMAGE onto Amphibimorph's AuraInterruptFlags, and a SpellMgr.cpp GetDiminishingReturnsLimitDuration case for family 19 / id 500952 returning 8 * IN_MILLISECONDS, following the exact existing precedent for two other custom classes' spells in the same function (Stone Grip 800145 family 37, Gaze of Ysera 806148 family 30 - the DR duration cap is a per-spell core list, not a broad engine limitation, so this is the smallest correct fix at that precedent's own layer). Before the fix: the dummy creature's aura survives the melee hit and the PvP victim keeps the aura for ~10 s (outside the asserted 7500-8000 ms band), so this scenario fails. After the fix: the dummy's aura is removed by the hit and the PvP victim's aura reads 7500-8000 ms. The 40 s duration against the non-player creature target is asserted as an unrelated regression guard: Unit::ApplyDiminishingToDuration only clamps duration when the target is a player (or a creature flagged CREATURE_FLAG_EXTRA_ALL_DIMINISH, which this fixture is not), so it must stay unclamped both before and after the fix. Amphibimorph has InterruptFlags 14, which includes SPELL_INTERRUPT_FLAG_INTERRUPT, so Spell::cast resets the doctor's swing timer to the Witch Doctor's 3200 ms main-hand attack time (attack_time_ms in witchdoctor-flat-percent-self-passives); the damage clause is therefore decided by a single white swing about 3190 ms after the attack, which is when every passing run saw the aura drop, and the next swing falls after the 6000 ms window. The dummy faces away from the doctor, so that swing can still miss or be dodged (5% each at equal level, with the weapon skill that AscensionCompat SynchronizeProficiencies maximizes for custom classes), and Unit::DealMeleeDamage skips DealDamage for an avoided swing; an accelerated run that lost that one roll kept the frog for the whole window. The doctor therefore carries melee_hit_rating and expertise_rating 10000, which remove only those avoidance rolls.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Amphibimorph lands on the hostile dummy creature
The frog transform applies to the dummy
BASELINE (native, regression guard): unclamped 40 sec duration against a non-player target, unaffected by the PvP duration-cap fix
Deal melee damage to the transformed dummy
#934 DISCRIMINATING: damage caused interrupts the effect
Amphibimorph has a 120 sec recovery time (Spell.dbc RecoveryTime); reset it so the second cast is not rejected SPELL_FAILED_NOT_READY
Amphibimorph lands on the PvP-flagged victim
The frog transform applies to the PvP victim
#934 DISCRIMINATING: PvP duration is capped to the tooltip's 8 sec instead of the generic 10 sec DR fallback
